purpose: Category-level research for the physical AI stack beyond GPUs: networking, optics, memory/HBM packaging, power reliability and industrial automation. Research-only; no site/UI/scoring changes.
categoryRead: The AI infrastructure bottleneck is broadening. Power and grid remain the dominant physical constraint, but current evidence now supports four additional gating layers: reliable backup power, data-centre/industrial networking, optical interconnect and HBM/advanced packaging. The macro regime is not permissive enough to buy every beneficiary: 4.7%+ long yields and weaker-credit stress favour companies with real orders, customer validation and manageable financing needs.

BDC.read: Best new quality/valuation combination. Record Q2 orders and explicit AI-data-centre plus physical-AI commentary show current commercial traction without the valuation of the hottest optical names.

GNRC.read: Roughly $1.6bn of data-centre backlog turns reliability into contracted hyperscaler demand. Keep below the top power/grid core until capacity-ramp economics and residential dilution are better understood.

AMKR.read: NVIDIA prepayment and a long-term TSMC partnership validate advanced packaging/testing as scarce AI infrastructure. Heavy capex and weak current FCF make it more rate-sensitive than BDC/GNRC.

0522.HK.role: HBM TCB/hybrid bonding + photonics + AI-server SMT
0522.HK.read: Strongest new Hong Kong/China candidate. It spans HBM, photonics and AI-server assembly with unusually strong booking evidence, but valuation and strategic-review execution require discipline.

existingCoreCrossRead.GEV: Generation/grid demand remains the highest-quality structural layer.
existingCoreCrossRead.ETN: Switchgear and power management remain a core rack-to-grid bottleneck.
existingCoreCrossRead.PWR: Transmission/substations remain essential for large-load interconnection.
existingCoreCrossRead.POWL: Order/backlog evidence is exceptional; valuation and execution remain the constraints.
existingCoreCrossRead.VRT: Cooling and power-management exposure remains strategically important but valuation discipline is required.
existingCoreCrossRead.ROK: Profitable factory/warehouse automation remains the preferred first-wave robotics/physical-AI expression.

opticsWatch.COHR: Fundamentals strong; do not chase while valuation remains elevated. Recent positioning unwind is attractive only if order/backlog trends stay intact.
opticsWatch.FN: Growth is strong but free-cash-flow conversion needs explanation before promotion.
opticsWatch.LITE: Continue monitoring laser/optical scarcity and customer concentration before adding another overlapping optical name.
opticsWatch.AAOI: Higher-beta optical watch; quality/valuation must beat existing candidates to justify admission.

memoryPackagingInterpretation: Reported AI-server price inflation tied to memory costs means HBM/DRAM scarcity can affect total server economics. Power Stack should therefore track not only memory producers but the scarce packaging, bonding, test and substrate infrastructure needed to integrate HBM with accelerators. AMKR and ASMPT are the strongest current research expressions from this layer.
powerReliabilityInterpretation: AI facilities increasingly need firm power around constrained grids. Backup generators, UPS/batteries, switchgear, voltage control, harmonic filtering and service/maintenance can monetise even when utility interconnection is delayed. Generac is the clearest new evidence that this adjacency has moved from theory to orders.
roboticsRead: No adoption-wave change. Fixed/warehouse automation remains first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, industrial humanoids third and open-world/general-purpose robots last. Belden's physical-AI networking exposure improves the picks-and-shovels layer without requiring a humanoid-OEM bet.
